title: Dynamic Commitment Negotiator and Graceful Fallback PRD
creator: Ravi Shah
description:
Problem: Customers using Redwood Dedicated report hard trade-offs between committing capacity (overpay) and relying on opportunistic burst capacity (risk of eviction/slowdowns). Current reserve models are static and do not expose fine-grained mechanisms for temporary leasing, negotiated headroom, or predictable fallbacks when contention occurs.

Goal: Design a Negotiator subsystem and accompanying UX/controls that allow tenants to request short-term committed headroom (leases), accept negotiated terms (price/eviction-priority/duration), and automatically fall back to deterministic degraded profiles when negotiations fail or evictions occur. The system must be predictable for both tenant SLAs and platform capacity planning.

Scope: This PRD covers product requirements for the Negotiator API, console UX flows, billing signals, and necessary scheduler hooks to implement lease grants and graceful degradation. It does not cover deep kernel/runtime optimizations or new hardware procurement.

Non-goals: Redesigning long-term reserved contracts, changing base pricing model, or exposing raw instance scheduling primitives to customers.
user_stories: As a platform engineer for an AI startup, I want to temporarily request 30% extra headroom for a 2-hour campaign so my inference pipelines don't degrade during a promotion.
As a reliability engineer, I want the system to guarantee clear fallback behaviors if the negotiated lease can't be honored so my application's latency SLOs are never silently violated.
As a finance lead, I want predictable billing estimates for leased headroom so I can approve bursts without unexpected cost spikes.
As an operator of Redwood, I want the system to provide eviction-priority signals and audit trails so we can enforce fairness and investigate incidents.
requirements: API: POST /v1/dedicated/leases to request a lease with params: tenant_id, requested_gpu_units, duration_minutes, max_price_per_minute, fallback_profile_id.
Negotiator: a policy engine that responds with Accept/Counter/Reject and proposed terms (granted_units, effective_price, eviction_priority, start_time, end_time).
Console: UI flow to request, review, and accept lease offers; show active leases and a cost estimate slider.
Scheduler hooks: ability to mark nodes as temporarily reserved for a tenant with a lease timebox and eviction priority metadata.
Fallback profiles: preconfigured degradation profiles (latency-oriented, cost-oriented, quality-oriented) tenant can select or provide as fallback.
Billing: prorated charges tied to granted_units and actual usage; plumbing for estimate and final invoice reconciliation.
Observability: telemetry for request->grant latency, lease fulfillment rate, preemption events, and per-tenant cost delta.
Audit: immutable audit record for each lease negotiation and acceptance with actor and timestamp.
Permissions: RBAC controls for who can request and approve leases within an organization.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end: A tenant can request a 60-minute lease for N units and receive an offer that can be accepted via API and console within 30s.
Fallback: If a lease is revoked or cannot be fulfilled, traffic is routed automatically to the tenant-selected fallback profile with explicit telemetry showing transition time and latency impact.
Billing: The invoice shows the negotiated price and prorated consumption; estimates shown in UI are within 5% of final charged amount for >=90% of leases in a 30-day window.
SLOs: For accepted leases, median tail latency (p95) for the tenant remains within their SLA contour for 95% of successful lease windows.
Observability: Lease lifecycle events (requested, offered, accepted, activated, revoked, completed) are emitted to the event log and visible in Console timelines.
Security: Only users with lease:request and lease:approve RBAC permissions can accept offers; audit logs reflect the approving principal.
metrics_and_success: Adoption: >= 15% of tier-2 and above Dedicated customers use leases within 3 months of launch.
Fulfillment: >= 92% of accepted leases must be fulfilled without preemption; remediations for failing leases must be automatic.
Cost predictability: 90th percentile difference between estimate and invoice <= 8% for leases > 30 minutes.
Operational overhead: Incidents attributable to lease negotiation <= 1 per quarter in the first year.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (alpha): Internal-only experiment with 3 pilot customers, feature-flagged scheduler hooks and console mockups (2 sprints).
Phase 1 (beta): Limited public beta for dedicated customers with opt-in billing statements and dedicated telemetry dashboards (4 sprints).
Phase 2 (general availability): Full launch with RBAC defaults, SLA language updates, and billing reconciliation improvements (2 sprints).
Fallback strategy: If leasing causes platform instability, automatically disable new leases and migrate active leases to conservative fallback profile while notifying customers.
open_questions: What are the economic guardrails for negotiated price floors vs. node utilization thresholds?
Do tenants get a hard guarantee on GPU count or a statistical SLA (e.g. 95% fulfilled minutes)?
How should negotiated eviction_priority map to existing fairshare/preemption systems?
Should fallback profile transitions be orchestrated by the tenant's client SDK or handled by the platform transparently?
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overcommitment of nodes leading to cascading preemptions. Mitigation: conservative default caps, simulated stress testing with synthetic workloads.
Risk: Unexpected billing disputes due to reconciliation lag. Mitigation: show clear estimate, keep separate lease-line items, provide 30-day audit window and dispute flow.
Risk: UX confusion around temporary vs reserved capacity. Mitigation: explicit labeling in Console, onboarding tooltips, and a short tutorial for early adopters.
communication_plan: Kickoff: cross-functional workshop to align on lease economics and eviction semantics.
Weekly: 30-minute sync during alpha/beta with rolling notes in Confluence.
Customer comms: beta announcement + documentation; post-GA webinar and migration guides.
notes: Scope was reduced on 2026-03-12 to remove support for multi-tenant blended leases; that will be a follow-up. Team decided to prioritize deterministic fallback behaviors over aggressive pricing experimentation in the first release.
final_acceptance_checklist: API contract reviewed and signed off by Eng & API standards
Console flows validated with 2 pilot customers
End-to-end telemetry and billing reconciliation smoke tests green
RBAC policies defined and integrated with org provisioning
